items.title: E1. Context and step latency
items.prompt: A loop begins with 3,000 tokens and appends 1,500 on each of 20 steps. Compare full-history prefill with prefix reuse and find final KV at 128 KiB/token. For one step, add prefill of 1,500 tokens for an 8.03B model at 495 TFLOP/s, decode of 90 tokens at 209.4 tok/s, and a 300 ms tool call.
items.answer:
*Solution.* Without reuse, step $i$ processes full history $3000+1500i$. The arithmetic progression gives $20\cdot3000+1500(0+\cdots+19)=345000$ tokens. Reuse processes initial prefix once and the 19 increments preceding calls once: $3000+19\cdot1500=31500$, a 10.9524 ratio of processed input positions, excluding the growing cost of reading old KV. Final KV is $33000\cdot128$ KiB = **4.0283 GiB**.

The conditional $2PT$ prefill estimate is $2\cdot8.03\text{B}\cdot1500/(495\text{ TFLOP/s})=48.667$ ms. Decode is $90/209.4=429.799$ ms and tool latency 300 ms. Total is **778.466 ms**, with decode at 55.21%. This is a conditional scenario without queueing or runtime overhead.

items.title: E2. Reliability and parallel accounting
items.prompt: Compute twenty-step success for step probabilities 0.98 and 0.95, without and with one independent retry. Find the per-step probability required for 90% success over 50 steps. Then analyze 20 subagents with 400 work minutes, 5 planning minutes, 20 merge minutes, 30K tokens per worker, and 128 KiB KV/token.
items.answer:
*Solution.* Without retry, every step must succeed: $0.98^{20}=0.66761$ and $0.95^{20}=0.35849$. With one independent retry, per-step success is $1-(1-p)^2$, or 0.9996 and 0.9975; raising these to the twentieth power gives **0.99203** and **0.95117**. Requiring $p^{50}=0.9$ gives $p=0.9^{1/50}=0.997895$.

Perfect partitioning makes worker time $400/20=20$ minutes and critical path $5+20+20=45$ minutes. Speedups are $400/45=8.89\times$ against useful work and $(5+400+20)/45=9.44\times$ end-to-end. Even infinitely many workers leave 25 serial minutes, imposing 16× and 17× ceilings. KV is $20\cdot30000\cdot128$ KiB = **73.242 GiB**. Retry independence and perfect partitioning are strong assumptions.

items.title: E3. CodeAct and a reproducible trace
items.prompt: Five JSON actions use 90 tokens each; one CodeAct block uses 160 tokens. Compute both ratios and interpret $150000/(2\cdot8.03\text{B})$. Then reproduce a trace that repairs a failed call and returns 27.92.
items.answer:
*Solution.* The JSON path uses $5\cdot90=450$ tokens and five model/tool round trips; CodeAct uses 160 tokens and one. The ratios are $450/160=\mathbf{2.8125\times}$ and $5/1=\mathbf{5\times}$. The value $150000/(2\cdot8.03\text{B})=9.33998\cdot10^{-6}$ compares 150K simple mask checks with rough $2P$ arithmetic for one model token; the work units differ, so the ratio is not a measured time fraction.

The reproducible trace first calls `lookup(sensor_bach)` and receives `tool_error`; it corrects the key to `sensor_batch` and obtains 13.96; then it calls the calculator with `13.96 * 2`, obtains 27.92, and returns `Answer: 27.92`. Event kinds are `assistant_action → tool_error → assistant_action → tool_result → assistant_action → tool_result → assistant_final → verification_pass`, with three registry invocations, one error, and status `completed`. The invariant is that the failure becomes an observation rather than uncontrolled execution.
